sources.entry: Atomic Server - Knowledge graph database with documents (similar to Notion), tables, search, and a powerful linked data API. Lightweight, very fast and no runtime dependencies. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker/Rust

summary.one_liner: Atomic Server is a self-hostable server for storage, search, sharing and sync of Atomic Data, part of a local-first workspace (atomic.place) for documents, tables, files, chat and apps.
summary.what_it_does: The repository covers the atomic.place browser workspace, the AtomicServer backend, the Atomic Data specification docs, and client libraries (@tomic/lib, @tomic/react, @tomic/svelte, atomic_lib in Rust, a Dart/Flutter client) plus a terminal client (atomic-cli). The README describes AtomicServer as the self-hostable component for storage, full-text search, sharing and sync, delivered as one binary (about 70MB) that bundles the web app, search, database and automatic HTTPS. Features listed for the workspace include documents, tables with schemas, kanban/calendar views, chat, meetings, canvas, websites, file uploads, and a REST API that returns JSON-AD, RDF, Turtle, N-Triples and JSON-LD. Data is versioned as signed commits and encrypted at rest on client devices. The README says the project is in alpha with breaking changes expected before 1.0.
use_cases: sync documents and tables across devices
linked data API for structured data
team collaboration on docs and tables
build apps backed by a personal data store
publish a website from a workspace
how_to_run: See the documentation at docs.atomicdata.dev for installation instructions (the README links to it but does not include commands).
notable: Single binary (~70MB) bundling server, web app, search, database and automatic HTTPS
Atomic Data spec with JSON-AD and RDF serializations (Turtle, N-Triples, JSON-LD)
Local-first sync with signed Atomic Commits and full version history
Full-text search with typeahead and fuzzy matching, same index on server and client
Client libraries for JavaScript, React, Svelte, Rust and Flutter
caveats: Status is alpha; breaking changes are expected until 1.0
The README does not include install commands; setup is in external documentation
Some features (AI via OpenRouter or Ollama, virtual drive) are tied to the desktop app or external services
